findings.explanation: Starting at the root README, the module registrations lead to gaze data, event labels and REMoDNaV; the latter explicitly registers the comparison dataset used by load_anderson. The consumed input paths make their relationships inspectable. Excluding regeneration of the raw acquisition dataset is a stated scope decision, not a silently repaired private link.

The analysis names the gaze and event-table paths and the nested annotated MAT files. Manuscript and analysis sources are root files. Missing payload bytes in this cohort do not negate inclusion by explicit reference, so the high boundary score is supported.

The root contains the runtime recipe and image registration; make targets, CLI defaults and classifier parameters supply the computation settings. This criterion does not demand immutable rebuilding, so the floating Debian package inputs do not by themselves lower this rating.

Module traversal exposes CC BY 4.0, MIT, PDDL and GPLv3 declarations. The frozen label-dataset inventory has no corresponding declaration. That concrete uncovered module supports partial fulfillment without asserting that unseen container payloads contain no licenses.

The inspected Git tree fixes source files and three root gitlinks; nested registrations and annex pointers identify data states, and the stored image manifest identifies configuration and layers. The mutable RepoTags label does not replace the image content identity. The rating is supported for the scoped distributed components.
findings.suggested_correction: Cite the root tree or Git tree probe alongside .gitmodules: .gitmodules stores locations, while gitlinks in the tree supply selected commit identities.

findings.explanation: The root Git tree, registered nested repositories and annex content keys form a compatible tracking view for the scoped code, inputs, image and outputs. Keeping payload storage outside Git does not break that tracked relationship.

The supplied reachable histories contain authors, timestamps and messages across the component classes. Root history records image conversion and manual diagram changes, and comparison-data history records relabeling. This supports attributable history without authenticating real-world author identity or proving every historical scientific activity was captured.

The historical records contain structured commands, inputs, outputs and exit status. The analysis dispatch does not call quality_stats, and the manuscript build appears as an instruction rather than a captured rendering run. Automatically captured provenance is therefore substantial but not comprehensive.

The central recorded run is associated with a root state and image input; the label-production record invokes a shell script and ordinary Python without recording an original environment state. This is a specific version-provenance gap supporting the partial anchor.

The cached tag object contains an armored signature and points to the result-run commit. The supplied documentation does not provide a signer-key authentication route, and cryptographic verification was not performed. The whole binary positive anchor is not established; zero does not mean that the tag is unsigned.

The clone/rerun instructions are backed by an input declaration covering comparison data, label tables, both gaze-data patterns and the image. The private acquisition submodule is not among those consumed inputs. The supplied acquisition procedure supports the rating independently of current download success.

The root supplies installation links and a subsequent clone/run sequence, but the linked installation pages are not frozen here. The inspected adapter explicitly assumes Docker can be managed by the invoking non-root user. P-01 treats that prerequisite as implicit, while A-02 states that no essential initialization or configuration decision remains. The frozen evidence does not settle that stronger operational claim.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify an inspected setup instruction that resolves Docker service access, or explain why the referenced installation procedure suffices under the evidence boundary. Otherwise use the partial setup anchor rather than claiming fully established operational completeness.

findings.explanation: The advertised command covers many results but omits quality_stats, whose output is used for the velocity figure and loss comparison. Its docstring does offer an instruction to edit dispatch, so it should not be described as wholly undocumented. The reference-only flowchart helper and absence of a complete result-to-command sequence for the full figure scope keep the limited rating defensible.
findings.suggested_correction: Explicitly distinguish the existing quality_stats integration note from a complete invocation sequence; identify the flowchart reconstruction gap as well if retaining the limited rather than partial anchor.

findings.explanation: The historical run lists both full gaze-data patterns, not just the example subjects, plus the nested comparison dataset, event tables and image. Those declarations support executable retrieval and composition. This is a specification judgment and does not imply that retrieval was tested.

The main statistical and rendering procedures are executable. Merely omitting a dispatcher call does not mean the quality-statistics algorithm needs translation from prose, because its body is supplied. However, the flowchart helper is reference-only, lacks output construction, and its local filter helper returns one coefficient object where the caller expects two. With figure regeneration included, a complete executable procedure is not established, supporting the partial rating.
findings.suggested_correction: Ground the partial score in the incomplete figure-generation procedure rather than treating the complete quality_stats function as an absent executable algorithm. Clarify whether preserving an authored SVG is an accepted input boundary for this figure.

findings.explanation: A named rerun target and a structured captured run supply replay support for the central analysis. The label run still leaves its original Python environment unresolved. The assessment appropriately avoids equating a replay command with demonstrated full historical replay.

Data repositories, algorithm source, analysis script, container directory, figure sources and manuscript have distinct roles and inspectable boundaries. A directory or file is sufficient here; separate packaging for every role is not required.

load_anderson reaches directly into REMoDNaV test-data internals, while other functions hard-code subject layouts and infer conversion settings from filenames. Independently versioned repositories therefore do not provide replaceable interfaces at configuration boundaries; the limited anchor is supported.

The MIT module declaration has explicit scope and the gaze dataset has its own PDDL declaration. No equivalent declaration appears in the inspected label module. A root license does not establish independent coverage of that linked repository, supporting partial module attribution.

The source exposes several component licenses but no object-specific treatment of their combinations. Generic license provisions cannot be substituted for recorded compatibility handling. The limited anchor is appropriate without making a legal incompatibility claim.

The rationale says that access conditions cannot be determined for all scoped components and that neither uniform nor mixed-access conditions can be established. M-05 explicitly assigns zero when access conditions cannot be determined. Unlike D-01, this criterion has a low anchor matching the stated uncertainty, so null incorrectly treats an applicable, assessable low-anchor case as unanswered. The omitted payloads alone also do not demonstrate an access restriction.
findings.suggested_correction: Use score 0 with a carefully bounded observation such as not_findable for the missing access-condition documentation, retaining the cohort limitation. If public acquisition documentation is judged enough to demonstrate uniform access, justify that alternative explicitly. Do not label evidence-package omission as an observed remote access failure; update completion metadata if the null becomes a scored judgment.

findings.explanation: The registered repository selections, fixed loader paths, image registration and Make/TeX relationships specify the consumed assembly. Weak replaceability does not make the composition implicit: fixed coupling can be explicit even while M-02 is low.

The README names orchestration tools and tested platforms and gives download sizes; the manuscript mentions memory requirements. The adapter itself documents an assumption of Docker access by a non-root user that the root instructions do not resolve explicitly. That concrete gap supports the partial host-prerequisite anchor.

The active run uses the current dataset mount and relative paths, derives UID/GID on non-Windows hosts and offers a Python command substitution. Fixed dataset-internal subject names are modularity constraints rather than host-specific paths. The old label-job submission configuration is not the active root procedure.
findings.suggested_correction: For the external adapter, accompany the version-tag URL with the frozen manifest checksum; a tag URL alone is not an immutable content locator.

findings.explanation: The inspected scientific imports are represented by the image recipe and REMoDNaV dependency declaration, including numerical, statistics and plotting libraries; LaTeX and Inkscape cover rendering. DataLad acquisition is host orchestration, with an explicit fallback in the container script. No identified active dependency is omitted by the cited specification.

Git tree inspection establishes that the image recipe and registration are tracked and that the algorithm dependency definition is in a fixed linked module. The binary criterion does not require frozen package resolution, so its positive value is justified.

The recipe, stored image and adapter are machine-consumable, but the assertion that there is no unresolved host-specific assumption conflicts with P-01 and the adapter comment about non-root Docker access. The top anchor requires explicit host configuration, and the frozen package does not contain the external setup instructions that might establish this condition.
findings.suggested_correction: Reconcile this with P-01. Supply inspected documentation resolving Docker service access, or use the partial machine-readable-environment anchor while that assumption remains unresolved. This is not evidence that Docker execution fails.

findings.explanation: The active root execution calls docker run using an ID computed from stored configuration bytes. It consequently creates a fresh container, rather than invoking an accumulated container session. The bind-mounted workspace and potentially retained temporary HOME are separate state-hygiene limits correctly relevant to E-03; this is source inspection, not a run observation.

The workspace is mounted outside container storage and the declared products and Git provenance persist there; docker run includes --rm. HOME cleanup occurs only after success, but retaining that diagnostic workspace directory does not make required results depend on keeping the container. Automatic container disposal supports the high anchor.

A clone and declared inputs establish the intended workspace, but clean does not reset the whole checkout and glob-based readers can include additional files. The fixed dockertmp directory can also survive a failed command. Automatic isolation to declared workspace inputs is not demonstrated, so the partial rating is reasonable.

The frozen references and annex availability metadata expose intended routes, but no payload acquisition was permitted or observed. None of the unavailable-version anchors is established by deliberate cache omission, and intended-version availability for every component is likewise unverified. Null preserves the genuine uncertainty here.

The raw-data README advertises deposit and alternative access routes, while the supplied image availability records point to one hosting service. A digest preserves identity, not bytes after host disappearance. The evidence does not establish preservation for every essential payload, so the limited rating is supported.

The base image is selected by a tag and apt installs resolve against moving package indexes without versions. Several exact pip pins do not fix the base or system packages. A useful build recipe exists, but it meets the moving-dependency anchor rather than reproducible reconstruction.

The inspected license texts have clear identities, but the label module still lacks a governing declaration. This specific omission suffices for partial fulfillment; unknown bundled image terms should remain an inspection limitation rather than an asserted absence inside uninspected layers.

The root tree jointly selects module commits, source/configuration states and a content-addressed image. The latest tag in Docker metadata is not the execution selector: the adapter selects image content identity. Current retrievability is appropriately separate under D-01.

The build history links a recipe input and image output, and a signed result tag exists, but neither is a supplied verifiable artifact attestation authenticating both producer and build source. The binary zero is supported; the result-tag signature must not be silently upgraded into verified image-origin evidence.

limitations: Independent inspection of only the assigned anonymized assessment, declared native instrument and frozen evidence cohort remodnav-e3c6253bced7; no peer assessments or reviews were consulted.

No scientific execution, builds, network requests or payload acquisition occurred. Binary figures, annex data and image layers were deliberately omitted; numerical equivalence, current availability and unseen payload contents remain unverified. Historical exit records are not review-time execution.

Read-only native validation passed. The assessment has 36 criterion responses with 34 assigned scores and two nulls, equal dimension weights, and fixed denominators; its provisional-completion comment is consistent with its current data. No supplied stored total contradicts native calculation. Replacing M-05 null with zero changes completion but not its provisional point contribution.

All 276 downloaded source/history/helper/availability records listed in the evidence manifest matched their recorded SHA256 values. This integrity check does not establish the truth or completeness of source claims.

External installation websites, README-linked discussion pages and remote signature-verification services were not visited. The external adapter was inspected only in its frozen supplied form; its version-tag URL is not itself a content-immutable locator.

Figure scope remains an interpretive boundary: preserving and rendering authored SVG sources differs from reconstructing their scientific plot components. A-03 and A-05 feedback identifies this distinction rather than claiming a failed run.
Actual runtime model identity was not independently observed and is left null. Agreement with a criterion is not human approval.
